You review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --face declaration` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35600: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #35620: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `ab09bb111fd18e8cc16540af7e8686a7b02c57c1`
  · the check-runs on `ab09bb111fd18e8cc16540af7e8686a7b02c57c1`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/4aece683-c91d-54c4-8fc9-e7eb31db7c45/scratchpad/35600/pr-35620/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ab09bb111fd18e8cc16540af7e8686a7b02c57c1`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #35600 body and its four comments (triage 7016233676, claim 7016332777, os-dev-report 7018093939, claim correction 7018227953); PR #35620 body, its 7 files, and the net diff against `main` (merge base `e25ca63e`); the check-runs on this head. Gates: none of the check-runs on the head failed: all read `success` or `skipped` except one. That `PR-body guards` run reads `cancelled` (workflow run 44588140969, 18:28:17Z); a later run of the same workflow on the same head (PR-Body Guards 44588242696, 18:28:52Z, after the body edit) reads `success`, and the check-run list carries that success too. Test UI 1-16/16, Type Check UI, Live E2E UI, Build and E2E UI, Check Changeset and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all `success`. That also settles the dev's flag that the folder sweep ran at `e0ccaad8` and not at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set change (Studio, client side): right.** On a read-only base, the object page's list-view Customize used to be gated only by `customizing && listViewTargetId !== null`. It now also requires `listViewServed.declaration !== null || listViewServed.shipped === 'base'` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` `listViewCustomizable`). That narrows what Studio offers to the set the server accepts. `overrideDraftBody` stamps `overrides` of the base, and the server refuses that stamp with `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` when the base ships no item of that name (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, the `closure.shippers` check). The client no longer offers a write the server would always refuse. This matches ADR-0146 D2 (an override declares an item the base ships) and D11 (a package-less row for an item no package ships is environment metadata, not an overlay). The server refusal is unchanged, and nothing that used to succeed is now withheld: the views that lose Customize (the environment row, a pair-added view, a default view the base does not ship) all answered 403 on their first save before this PR.
- **The fact the gate reads: right.** `useServedOverride` already made the layered read at the base. `shipped` is computed from that same response (`code != null` gives `base`, else `overlay != null` gives `environment`, else `none`), so there is no new request. I checked the 404 path: `MetadataClient.layered()` resolves the server's 404 as all layers null (as noted in `ResourceEditPage.tsx` `holdsNoLayer` and `usePublishAllDrafts.ts` `holdsNoPublishedLayer`). So a pair-added view really gets `none` and not `null`, and the test double's all-null answer matches the real client. A view the pair's draft already overrides returns `shipped: null` with a declaration, and it stays customizable through the declaration arm. The hook keys its answer without the nonce, so the re-read after the first save into the pair keeps the last answer and the gate does not flicker.
- **Fail-closed behaviour: right, and disclosed.** A failed layered read returns `NO_OVERRIDE` (`shipped: null`), so a base view loses Customize until a read succeeds, stays read-only and writes nothing. The PR's Verification section names this risk. Nit: on the first open of a view, Customize and the specific note wait for the read, and the generic read-only sentence shows in the meantime. Cosmetic only.
- **Other callers of `useServedOverride` (leaf, nav, flow, `StudioBundleItemEditor`): unaffected.** Their declaration and state values are the same as before. The only difference is the extra `shipped` field, which they ignore.
- **Public surface: right.** `@object-ui/i18n` gains two keys, `engine.studio.inspector.listView.environmentView` and `engine.studio.inspector.listView.notShipped`, in both en and zh with the same `{package}` placeholder. That widens the published key set. In `@object-ui/app-shell` (a private package, versioned under `privatePackages`), `ServedOverride.shipped` and the `ObjectListViewInspector` `readOnlyNote` prop are not exported from `src/index.ts` (only `StudioDesignSurface` is), so app-shell's public surface does not change. No spec key, accepted value or metadata type changes.
- **Test: adequate.** `InterfacesPillar.customizePackagelessView-35600.test.tsx` mounts the real pillar and header controls over a server double whose draft door returns the measured 403. The environment arm pins the gate (the dev's ablation turns it red). The `none` arm pins only the note, as the dev disclosed. The CONTROL arm pins that a base view still customizes with `overrides: { package, basedOn }`. Nit: no arm on its own pins the gate for a `none` view. The environment arm already covers the predicate.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: the two new i18n keys widen the published `@object-ui/i18n` key set. The PR body and the changeset body both carry it as a line-initial declaration, together with `Metadata-protocol: none`. This matches the seat's claim correction 7018227953 and replaces the claim's original `Clause-②: no`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- Level `patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` is right. Under AGENTS.md, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The changeset names both packages the diff moves, it is not `skip-changeset`, and no breaking arm applies, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0]** (should the object page edit a pair-added list view in the pair, as the rail does): **answered: A**, keep it read-only on the object page. This is my own judgment, not the seat's. The card is about views the deployment created, and B is a new write path that needs a second fact (the view's served package) which the card does not settle. A also regresses nothing: such a view used to answer 403 from the object page, and the rail's Form and list views entry still edits it in the pair.
- **Deviation: Clause-② re-declared:** answered above (②). The record on the card and the head agree.
- **Deviation: file surface widened to `ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/{en,zh}.ts`:** answered. Claim correction 7018227953 covers both files, and they hold only the two strings.
- **Deviations: commit trailers, PR footer, worktree re-point:** answered, no contract effect. The five commits carry the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair and the session URL, and the PR body carries the footer.
- **Deviation: test-tree reach (folder sweep at `e0ccaad8`):** answered. The head's 16 Test UI shards are green.
- **out_of_scope_findings:** the draft-preview bar observation is filed as #35624, so it has a carrier. The default view the base does not ship is no longer customizable from the object page: answered, not a regression (it answered 403 before), and making it a new pair item is a product choice that needs its own card if wanted.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):** no finding. The diff is Studio UI only. It adds no data query, no id materialisation and no in-app join, and the gate reuses a metadata read that the hook already made.
- **security_findings:** none reported, and none found in this review.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：在只读基础包上，Studio 对象页只对基础包自己带的列表视图提供「定制」。在应用里新建的视图不再出现一点「定制」、一保存就 403 的情况。这类视图在 Studio 里只读，面板会说明要到应用里的「管理视图 › 编辑视图配置」去改。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是某个基础包确实带的视图读取失败时，暂时不显示「定制」。这时只是不能改，不会写错东西。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事，区域自己落地。

  - The note appears only when the view is asked about, there is no declaration, and the read answered `environment` or `none`.
  - A failed read gives `shipped: null`. Customize is then withheld and the generic read-only line shows, which fails closed.
  - That matches ADR-0146 D2 and D11, which the claim read as binding.
- **What the gate withholds was refused before.** The environment row, a pair-added view and a synthesized default view the base does not ship each answered 403 on their first save, so no working path is lost. The pair-added view stays editable from the rail.

Record 7018899204 is **PASS on this head** (`ab09bb11`) with no must-fix or should-fix, and I adopt it. It also checked that a 404 from `layered()` reads as all layers null, so `none` is real. Its two nits are accepted: the generic line shows while the read is in flight, and no arm pins the gate on its own for a `none` view.
